Refit a factorised hurdle model as a single joint fit

Source: R/bnec_joint.R
bnec_joint.Rd

Takes the model combination favoured by crossed_weights and refits it as one bnec model with a two-block (hurdle_gamma or zero_inflated_beta) family.

bnec_joint(object, model = NULL, model_survival = NULL, formula = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

An object of class bayesnechurdlefit returned by bnec_hurdle.

model

An optional character string naming the equation for the response block. Defaults to the highest-weighted growth model in object.

model_survival

An optional character string naming the equation for the survival block. Defaults to the highest-weighted survival model in object.

formula

An optional bayesnecformula to fit instead of the one held in object. Supply this to add structure the factorised fit cannot carry, for example a group-level term. The crf model argument is overwritten by model either way.

...

Further arguments passed to bnec.

Value

An object of class bayesnecfit.

Details

Why refit at all

The factorised and joint routes give equivalent inference where the two components are independent, so a joint refit of the same pair of equations adds nothing on its own – the estimates differ only by Monte Carlo noise. What it adds is the ability to write structure that spans the two blocks, which the factorisation cannot express by construction: a group-level effect shared between response and survival makes the two posteriors dependent, and a dependent posterior cannot be assembled from two fits run separately.

The division of labour is therefore: fit the model sets with bnec_hurdle, where all n_growth * n_survival combinations can be compared from two fits; choose a combination from crossed_weights; then refit that one jointly here, adding the shared structure. Model averaging happens in the first step, because the joint route can only average over the response block.

What is carried over

The response variable, predictor and data are taken from object, and the family follows the growth component: hurdle_gamma where that was fitted as a Gamma, zero_inflated_beta where it was a Beta. Nothing else transfers – priors, control arguments and the like are defaults again unless passed through ....

See also

bnec_hurdle, crossed_weights, best_crossed, bnec

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(bayesnec)
data(nec_data)
nec_data$y[nec_data$x > 2.5] <- 0
nec_data$tank <- factor(rep(1:10, length.out = nrow(nec_data)))
fit <- bnec_hurdle(y ~ crf(x, c("nec3param", "nec4param", "ecx4param")),
                   data = nec_data)
# the pair crossed_weights() favours, refitted as one model
fit_j <- bnec_joint(fit)
# the same pair with a group-level effect the factorisation cannot carry
fit_r <- bnec_joint(fit, formula = y ~ crf(x, "nec3param") + (nec | tank))
} # }
